As an employer who works in a federaly regulated "safety sensitive" industry. I have mixed feelings on it. Preemployment is more ok to me than random testing. For randoms when someone fails you don't get to just fire them. Each state is different but most are similar, and if its a federal test the state doesn't matter. Sure many companies do fire you imideatly, and since most employees don't know what's legal don't know any better.

Sometimes when someone fails they quit because they wrongly assume you are going to fire them. For a failed DOT test they get assigned an SAP who prescribes treatment. You have to guarantee their position during the treatment. Only if they fail to fulfill their requirements during treatment can you terminate the employment. Who pays for the treatment varies, sometimes the employees insurance will cover it (rare and first timers only), some states make the employer cover it, others leave it to the employee.

You see a huge variation in what treatment is prescribed. I'm not sure if the SAPs are using some aspect of the results or if its more subjective. For THC I have seen ranges from 1 season of therapy to 2 years worth of weekly meetings. Now most people can't sit around for 2 years, so quit and look for another job. Problem with the federal testing is until you finish that perscribed therapy your blacklisted from any federally regulated position.
